title: Amazon Alexa won't stop saying 'lalala' and users are creeped out (Updated: Fix incoming)
source_used: Android Authority (full text from the fulltext folder, including its update of 5 Oct 2026, 11:56 PM ET)
key_facts: Android Authority's original article (5 Oct 2026, 11:34 AM ET) says that over the last month users have reported Alexa getting stuck repeating the word 'la' over and over.
According to those user reports, Alexa keeps saying it for several minutes before it stops; the article embeds a video example.
Update (5 Oct 2026, 11:56 PM ET): Amazon confirmed to Android Authority that the problem was a bug affecting 'a small number of Alexa Plus' users, and that it is in the process of implementing a fix.
The cause is not stated; some users blame a recent update; Android Authority had asked Amazon for comment.
A couple of months earlier users were taken aback when Alexa made guttural sounds like a snarling animal.
The article also notes that Gemini, Google's assistant, refused to answer questions on Android Auto the previous week.
quote_evidence: Amazon has now confirmed to Android Authority that Alexa’s strange affliction was indeed a bug impacting “a small number of Alexa Plus” users.
It appears the AI will get stuck repeating the word “la” over and over again.
It’s unclear what’s causing Alexa to meltdown like this, but some users are blaming a recent update.
why_it_matters_hint: A mainstream AI assistant glitched in people's homes for about a month before the maker confirmed a bug; cause, scale and fix date are not given.
event_date: User reports over about a month; Amazon's confirmation late on 5 Oct 2026 (US Eastern time)
notes: Amazon's confirmation reached the article as an update at 11:56 PM ET on 5 Oct 2026, so the news is new in the window although the glitch reports run back about a month. The 'la' symptom and 'several minutes' come from user reports, not from Amazon. The article does not explain what Alexa Plus is; it treats it as Amazon's AI-based assistant.
